content.content:
1	"""Deterministic 2D grid A* planner.
2	
3	Public entry points: ``plan(width, height, blocked, start, goal, costs=None,
4	trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
5	max_cost=None, allow_wait=False, dynamic_costs=None, reservations=None)``,
6	``plan_any(width, height, blocked,
7	start, goals, costs=None, trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None,
8	max_expanded=None, snapshot=False, max_cost=None, allow_wait=False,
9	dynamic_costs=None, reservations=None)``,
10	``plan_k(width, height, blocked, start, goal, k, costs=None,
11	dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, max_cost=None,
12	allow_wait=False, dynamic_costs=None, reservations=None)``,
13	``plan_batch(width, height, blocked, requests, costs=None, trace=False,
14	dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
15	max_cost=None, allow_wait=False, dynamic_costs=None, reservations=None)``,
16	``plan_multi_start(width, height, blocked, starts, goal, costs=None,
17	trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
18	max_cost=None, allow_wait=False, dynamic_costs=None, reservations=None)``,
19	``replay(width, height, blocked, start, goal, path, costs=None,
20	dynamic_blocked=None, diagnose=False, allow_wait=False,
21	dynamic_costs=None, reservations=None)``,
22	``resume(checkpoint, max_expanded=None)``,
23	``distance_field(width, height, blocked, goal, costs=None, trace=False)``,
24	``distance_field_any(width, height, blocked, goals, costs=None,
25	trace=False)`` and
26	``verify_trace(width, height, blocked, start, goal, record, costs=None,
27	dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False, max_cost=None,
28	allow_wait=False, dynamic_costs=None, reservations=None)``.
29	
30	Semantics:
31	- Four-neighborhood moves, Manhattan heuristic. Without ``costs`` each step
32	  has unit cost. With ``costs`` (a height-by-width matrix of positive
33	  integers, row-major: ``costs[y][x]``) entering a cell costs that cell's
34	  value; the start cell's cost is never counted, so ``cost`` is the sum of
35	  the costs of the cells entered along the path.
36	- Tie-breaking is fully specified and order-independent: compare f, then h,
37	  then the (x, y) coordinate in lexicographic order.
38	- ``expanded`` counts exactly the nodes popped from the priority queue and
39	  closed for the first time (the goal counts when reached; stale heap
40	  entries and duplicate closings do not).
41	- Returns ``{"path": [...], "cost": int, "expanded": int}`` on success and
42	  ``{"path": None, "cost": None, "expanded": int}`` when unreachable.
43	- When ``trace`` is true, both kinds of results additionally include
44	  ``expanded_nodes``: the list of coordinate tuples closed for the first
45	  time, in expansion order (includes the start, and the goal on success);
46	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)``. The field is omitted entirely when
47	  ``trace`` is false or omitted.
48	
49	Search budget (``max_expanded``):
50	- ``max_expanded`` may be omitted or ``None``, which keeps every key,
51	  value, exception type and validation order of the default behavior
52	  untouched. Otherwise it must be a non-negative integer that is not a
53	  bool: other types raise ``TypeError`` and negative values raise
54	  ``ValueError``. These checks run after all existing grid, costs,
55	  ``trace`` and ``dynamic_blocked`` validation (including the frame-0
56	  check) and before the search starts.
57	- The budget counts closed nodes (exactly what ``expanded`` counts); once
58	  the limit is reached no further node is closed. When the budget is
59	  provided the result always carries an additional ``status`` field:
60	  ``"found"`` when the goal was closed within the limit (the usual
61	  ``path``/``cost`` are returned), ``"unreachable"`` when the candidates
62	  were exhausted without reaching the goal, and ``"budget_exhausted"``
63	  when live candidates remained but the budget stopped the search (then
64	  ``path``/``cost`` are ``None`` and ``expanded`` is the actual closed
65	  count, at most ``max_expanded``).
66	- The budget applies identically in static and dynamic mode and never
67	  changes expansion order, path choice, trace entries or determinism: a
68	  budgeted trace is a prefix of the unbudgeted one. With ``trace=True``
69	  only actually closed nodes are recorded, so a zero budget records
70	  nothing -- even when ``start == goal`` a zero budget returns
71	  ``budget_exhausted`` with ``expanded == 0``; the single-point success
72	  result requires at least one closed node (``max_expanded >= 1``).
73	- ``replay`` is unaffected: it keeps validating candidate paths only and
74	  accepts no budget parameter.
75	
76	Cost limit (``max_cost``):
77	- ``max_cost`` may be omitted or ``None``, which keeps every key, value,
78	  exception type and validation order of the previous behavior untouched.
79	  Otherwise it must be a non-negative integer that is not a bool: other
80	  types raise ``TypeError`` and negative values raise ``ValueError``. The
81	  check runs after all existing grid, costs, ``trace``, ``dynamic_blocked``,
82	  ``max_expanded`` and ``snapshot`` validation and before the search
83	  starts.
84	- The limit caps the accumulated entering-cell cost of a route, measured
85	  from the start (the start cell still costs 0 and each entered cell costs
86	  its ``costs`` value, or 1 without ``costs``). A candidate whose
87	  accumulated cost would exceed the limit is discarded; a candidate at
88	  exactly the limit still competes. The limit applies identically in
89	  static mode, dynamic mode and ``plan_any``, and never changes expansion
90	  order, tie-breaks, the minimum-cost choice, the multi-goal endpoint
91	  comparison or trace entries.
92	- When ``max_cost`` is provided the result always carries ``status``:
93	  ``"found"`` on success, and on failure ``"cost_exhausted"`` when at
94	  least one candidate was discarded for exceeding the limit, otherwise
95	  ``"unreachable"`` (``path``/``cost`` are ``None`` and ``expanded``
96	  counts the actually closed nodes). When ``max_expanded`` is also given,
97	  a budget stop still takes priority with ``"budget_exhausted"``.
98	  ``trace`` keeps recording only actually closed nodes, and the
99	  ``start == goal`` single-point zero-cost result and the zero-budget
100	  rules are unchanged.
101	- With ``snapshot=True`` the checkpoint records the ``max_cost`` value
102	  when one was provided (and no new field when it was not). ``resume``
103	  treats a checkpoint without the field as ``None``, validates a present
104	  field with the same rules (``TypeError`` for wrong types, ``ValueError``
105	  for negative values or a state inconsistent with the limit) before any
106	  searching, and a resumed search is equivalent to one uninterrupted call
107	  with the same limit. ``replay`` accepts no ``max_cost`` parameter.
108	
109	Waiting in place (``allow_wait``):
110	- ``plan``, ``plan_any``, ``plan_batch``, ``plan_multi_start``, ``plan_k``
111	  and ``replay`` accept a final optional boolean ``allow_wait`` that
112	  defaults to ``False``. ``False`` -- or an omitted, ``None`` or empty
113	  ``dynamic_blocked`` -- keeps every key, value, exception type,
114	  validation order, four-neighborhood move, no-repeated-coordinate rule
115	  and tie-break of the previous behavior untouched. A non-bool
116	  ``allow_wait`` raises ``TypeError`` after the ``dynamic_blocked``
117	  checks (the frame-0 check included) and before the budget and snapshot
118	  checks; every other exception type and order is unchanged.
119	- With ``allow_wait=True`` a route may stay in its current cell from
120	  time ``t`` to time ``t + 1`` provided the cell is not blocked at frame
121	  ``t + 1``. Waiting adds no entering-cell cost (``cost`` still sums
122	  only the cells entered by moves, and ``max_cost`` caps only those) and
123	  is only generated while ``t + 1`` lies within the provided frames:
124	  after the last frame the last frame is still reused for moves but no
125	  further waits are generated. Consecutive waits repeat the same
126	  coordinate in the path; once a cell is left it may never be
127	  re-entered. ``start == goal`` still yields only the single-point
128	  zero-cost route.
129	- The minimum-cost choice, the endpoint selection and the complete-path
130	  lexicographic tie-break follow the existing rules, with the priority
131	  still f, then h, then the coordinate, then the time and finally the
132	  complete path, so results never depend on obstacle-set or in-frame
133	  iteration order. Wait states count toward ``expanded`` one per closing
134	  and the trace records their ``(x, y, t)`` triples; ``max_expanded``
135	  truncates them like any other state and the ``status`` values and
136	  priorities are unchanged. ``plan_k``, ``plan_batch``, multi-goal and
137	  multi-start results follow the same waiting semantics, and a
138	  successful path verifies in ``replay`` with the same cost and step
139	  count, the waits included in ``steps``.
140	- ``replay`` with ``allow_wait=True`` accepts consecutive stays only
141	  within the provided dynamic frames; stays in static mode or without
142	  frames, stays after the final frame and non-consecutive revisits all
143	  return the usual invalid structure. With ``diagnose=True`` a stay
144	  after the final frame reports the dedicated error
145	  ``wait_after_final_frame``.
146	- A budget-exhausted checkpoint records ``allow_wait`` when it was true
147	  and ``resume`` of such a checkpoint is equivalent to one uninterrupted
148	  call with the same setting. Checkpoints written without the field
149	  restore it as ``False``; a present non-bool field raises ``TypeError``
150	  and a field inconsistent with the recorded internal state raises
151	  ``ValueError``.
152	
153	Dynamic obstacles (``dynamic_blocked``):
154	- ``dynamic_blocked`` may be omitted, ``None`` or an empty sequence, which
155	  leaves the static behavior above untouched. Otherwise it must be a
156	  sequence of frames; each frame is an iterable of grid coordinates that
157	  are blocked at that time frame. Frame 0 constrains ``start``; the
158	  coordinate at path index ``t`` must avoid both the static obstacles and
159	  frame ``t``, and frames beyond the last one reuse the last frame.
160	- Moves are still four-neighborhood only: no waiting in place and no
161	  repeated coordinates along the path. Because feasibility of a route
162	  depends on the coordinates it already visited, candidates that reach the
163	  same ``(x, y, t)`` through different coordinate histories are distinct
164	  states and are never merged: every route that satisfies the constraints
165	  can be explored. ``cost`` is still the sum of the costs of the cells
166	  entered; the start cell is never counted.
167	- The minimum-cost feasible route is returned. When total costs tie, the
168	  fixed priority is f, then h, then x, y, t, and candidates still tied are
169	  ordered lexicographically by their complete coordinate sequence, so the
170	  result never depends on the iteration order of the obstacle sets, the
171	  coordinates inside a frame, or the traversal order.
172	- In dynamic mode ``expanded_nodes`` records ``(x, y, t)`` triples in
173	  actual closing order and ``expanded`` counts closed space-time route
174	  states one per entry; a discarded candidate is never recorded. When the
175	  same ``(x, y, t)`` is closed through different histories, its triple
176	  appears once per closing in closing order, and ``expanded`` counts each
177	  such entry. On failure ``path``/``cost`` are ``None``.
178	- Validation: the outer value must be a sequence and every frame an
179	  iterable of coordinates; strings/bytes and non-two-integer coordinates
180	  raise ``TypeError``, out-of-bounds coordinates raise ``ValueError``,
181	  duplicates within a frame are merged, and a ``start`` blocked at frame 0
182	  raises ``ValueError``. All checks run before the search starts.
183	
184	Time-varying costs (``dynamic_costs``):
185	- ``plan``, ``plan_any``, ``plan_batch``, ``plan_multi_start``,
186	  ``plan_k`` and ``replay`` accept a final optional
187	  ``dynamic_costs=None`` parameter. Omitting it, passing ``None`` or an
188	  empty sequence keeps every result key, exception boundary, expansion
189	  order, path choice and the legacy ``costs`` semantics of the previous
190	  behavior untouched; every other entry point keeps its signature.
191	- Otherwise ``dynamic_costs`` must be a sequence of height-by-width
192	  matrices of positive integers, one matrix per time frame. An outer
193	  value or frame that is not an acceptable sequence, or a cell that is
194	  not a non-bool integer, raises ``TypeError``; a wrong row or column
195	  count, a non-positive cost, or providing both ``costs`` and
196	  ``dynamic_costs`` raises ``ValueError``. All checks run after every
197	  pre-existing validation (in ``plan_batch`` before any request is
198	  searched) and before the search starts.
199	- When enabled, entering a coordinate at path index ``t`` costs that
200	  cell's value in frame ``t``; the start cell is still never charged and
201	  frames beyond the last one reuse the last frame. Waiting follows the
202	  existing rules and never produces an entering-cell cost. The search
203	  returns the globally minimum total ``cost`` route under the static and
204	  dynamic obstacle constraints; equal costs are still arbitrated by the
205	  existing endpoint and complete-path lexicographic rules, and
206	  ``expanded``/``expanded_nodes`` count only actually closed space-time
207	  states: distinct histories are never merged and no out-of-bounds,
208	  blocked or illegally repeated nodes are generated.
209	- ``max_cost`` caps the dynamic accumulated cost with the usual
210	  ``cost_exhausted`` and budget-priority rules; ``plan_any``'s winning
211	  endpoint rules, the trace shape, the ``start == goal`` result and
212	  unreachable results are unchanged. ``plan_batch`` answers each
213	  request exactly as an independent ``plan`` call with the same frames;
214	  ``plan_multi_start`` picks its winner by the same total-cost and
215	  complete-path tie-breaks and records ``(x, y, t)`` trace triples in
216	  dynamic mode; ``plan_k`` ranks its unique routes by the dynamic
217	  accumulated cost with the usual truncation and status rules.
218	  ``replay`` recomputes ``cost``
219	  with the same frames, so a legal path matches the planning result;
220	  the diagnostic error types and the ``steps`` rule are unchanged.
221	- With ``snapshot=True`` the checkpoint records ``dynamic_costs`` as a
222	  JSON-serializable structure (the field is omitted when they were not
223	  provided) together with the waiting setting, the accumulated state and
224	  the cost limit when one was provided; a resumed search matches one
225	  uninterrupted call field by field, the next checkpoint included. A
226	  checkpoint whose ``dynamic_costs`` is corrupt raises ``TypeError`` or
227	  ``ValueError`` and never silently degrades. ``plan_k`` accepts no
228	  snapshot option.
229	
230	Reserved space-time routes (``reservations``):
231	- ``plan``, ``plan_any``, ``plan_batch``, ``plan_multi_start``,
232	  ``plan_k`` and ``replay`` accept a final optional
233	  ``reservations=None`` parameter for multi-robot coordination.
234	  Omitting it, passing ``None`` or an empty sequence keeps every result
235	  key, exception type, validation order, expansion order and tie-break
236	  of the previous behavior untouched; existing calls need no changes.
237	- Otherwise ``reservations`` must be a sequence of non-empty coordinate
238	  paths, each the timed route another agent already occupies. An outer
239	  value or path that is not an acceptable sequence, or a coordinate
240	  that is not exactly two integers, raises ``TypeError``; an empty
241	  path, an out-of-bounds coordinate, a coordinate on a static obstacle
242	  or a coordinate repeated non-consecutively within one path raises
243	  ``ValueError``. Consecutive stays inside a reservation path are
244	  kept. Duplicate routes merge and the entry order never influences
245	  any result. All checks run after every pre-existing validation (in
246	  ``plan_batch`` before any request is searched) and before the search
247	  starts.
248	- A path's t-th coordinate occupies that vertex at frame ``t``; past
249	  the final coordinate the last one persists. Each pair of adjacent
250	  coordinates forms the directed edge of that frame. A candidate route
251	  may not enter a reserved vertex at the same frame, nor traverse the
252	  reverse of a reserved edge between two frames. The candidate remains
253	  subject to the static obstacles, ``dynamic_blocked``, ``costs`` and
254	  ``dynamic_costs`` exactly as before, and reservations alone already
255	  make the search time-expanded.
256	- With ``allow_wait=True`` a route may wait in place at frames that are
257	  safe (the cell is neither blocked nor reserved at the next frame);
258	  waiting adds no entering-cell cost and is only generated while the
259	  next time step still lies within the provided frames (dynamic
260	  obstacle frames and reservation frames each provide them). Once a
261	  cell is left it may never be re-entered non-consecutively.
262	- Route selection keeps the dynamic-mode adjudication: smallest total
263	  ``cost``, then the arrival step count, then the complete coordinate
264	  sequence lexicographically. ``expanded`` counts only actually closed
265	  space-time states and ``trace`` records ``(x, y, t)`` triples; an
266	  unreachable query returns the usual empty-path result. A start
267	  reserved at frame 0 roots no feasible route.
268	- ``max_expanded``, ``max_cost``, ``plan_k``, ``plan_batch`` and
269	  ``plan_multi_start`` keep their ``status``, truncation and
270	  independent-query semantics. With ``snapshot=True`` the checkpoint
271	  records the normalized reservations (the field is omitted when they
272	  were not provided), and ``resume`` of such a checkpoint matches one
273	  uninterrupted call field by field; a checkpoint whose
274	  ``reservations`` is corrupt raises ``TypeError`` or ``ValueError``.
275	- ``replay`` re-checks a candidate path against the same reservations:
276	  a successful path verifies with the same ``cost`` and ``steps``.
277	  With ``diagnose=True`` a path entering a reserved vertex reports
278	  ``reservation_vertex`` and a path traversing a reserved edge in
279	  reverse reports ``reservation_edge``, each with the zero-based index
280	  of the first offending element; every other invalid path keeps the
281	  existing fixed structure and error codes.
282	
283	Multi-goal planning (``plan_any``):
284	- ``plan_any(width, height, blocked, start, goals, ...)`` accepts the same
285	  grid, blocked, start, costs, trace, dynamic_blocked and max_expanded
286	  arguments as ``plan``, plus a non-empty ``goals`` sequence of candidate
287	  endpoint coordinates. It returns one deterministic minimum-cost route to
288	  any of the candidates, in the same result structure as ``plan``; the
289	  path's last point is the winning endpoint.
290	- The grid, costs, trace, dynamic-blocked and budget checks run in
291	  ``plan``'s order with the same exception types; ``goals`` takes
292	  ``goal``'s position in that sequence. The outer value must be a
293	  sequence: strings, bytes, ``None`` and other non-sequences raise
294	  ``TypeError`` and an empty sequence raises ``ValueError``. Each endpoint
295	  follows the coordinate structure and integer rules (bad shape or
296	  coordinate types raise ``TypeError``); out-of-bounds coordinates and
297	  endpoints on static obstacles raise ``ValueError``. Repeated candidates
298	  merge, so the input ordering never changes any result.
299	- The search keeps four-neighborhood moves, no waiting, no revisits, the
300	  persistent last frame and the entering-cell cost accumulation. A
301	  candidate blocked by the dynamic frame at the time a particular route
302	  arrives is not rejected up front (its coordinate is statically valid);
303	  that arrival is simply infeasible for that route's time frame while
304	  other arrival times still compete.
305	- Total ``cost`` decides; ties compare the endpoint coordinate ``(x, y)``
306	  lexicographically, then the complete coordinate path lexicographically.
307	  As in dynamic ``plan``, routes reaching the same cell through different
308	  coordinate histories are distinct states and are never merged, so the
309	  traversal is a best-first walk of the feasible route tree; expansion
310	  order and the trace never depend on goal order, the blocked sets or
311	  in-frame iteration order. A budget never replaces an already determined
312	  better route with a worse one.
313	- When no endpoint is reachable, ``path`` and ``cost`` are ``None``. With a
314	  budget the ``status`` field follows the same ``"found"``,
315	  ``"unreachable"`` and ``"budget_exhausted"`` rules, and ``trace`` only
316	  records actually closed nodes: coordinate pairs in static mode and
317	  ``(x, y, t)`` triples in dynamic mode. A ``goals`` containing ``start``
318	  yields the single-point zero-cost route under the same start-equals-goal
319	  and zero-budget rules as ``plan``. A successful path verifies offline in
320	  ``replay`` when its last point is passed as ``goal``, with the same cost
321	  and step count.
322	
323	Top-k planning (``plan_k``):
324	- ``plan_k(width, height, blocked, start, goal, k, costs=None,
325	  dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, max_cost=None,
326	  allow_wait=False, dynamic_costs=None)`` returns
327	  several distinct feasible routes on the same grid in one call. It
328	  first performs exactly ``plan``'s shared validation for the
329	  dimensions, coordinates, static obstacles, positive integer cost
330	  matrix and dynamic frames (including the frame-0 start check), and
331	  only then checks ``k``: a non-bool positive integer is required,
332	  wrong types raise ``TypeError`` and non-positive values raise
333	  ``ValueError``. The optional ``max_expanded`` and ``max_cost``
334	  limits are checked after all of that (the ``k`` check included),
335	  still before the search starts, with the same non-negative,
336	  non-bool integer rules ``plan`` uses (other types raise
337	  ``TypeError``, negative values raise ``ValueError``). The optional
338	  ``dynamic_costs`` frames are validated after all of those checks,
339	  still before the search starts, with the shared time-varying cost
340	  rules (providing both ``costs`` and ``dynamic_costs`` raises
341	  ``ValueError``). Every error is
342	  decided before the search starts, and ``plan_k`` accepts no
343	  ``trace`` or ``snapshot`` argument.
344	- The search keeps four-neighborhood moves, the zero start cost, the
345	  entering-cell cost accumulation, the persistent last frame, the ban on
346	  waiting in place and on repeated coordinates, and the static/frame
347	  feasibility rules. Routes that reach the same cell through different
348	  coordinate histories are distinct candidates and are never merged, in
349	  both static and dynamic mode, so different complete coordinate
350	  sequences always remain separate results.
351	- It returns ``{"paths": [...], "costs": [...], "expanded": int}``: at
352	  most ``k`` unique complete routes ordered by ascending total cost and,
353	  on ties, by the lexicographic order of the complete coordinate
354	  sequence; ``costs`` corresponds to ``paths`` entry by entry. The first
355	  entry is the route ``plan`` would return. When no route is feasible
356	  both lists are empty and ``expanded`` still reports the route
357	  candidates actually closed to determine the answer: one count per
358	  complete history, and never counting a candidate filtered at
359	  generation or left pending. The traversal stops the moment the k-th
360	  goal route has been closed, so a small k closes strictly fewer
361	  candidates than a larger one. ``start == goal`` yields only the
362	  single-point zero-cost route, with one expansion. Every returned route
363	  verifies offline in ``replay`` with the same cost and step count, in
364	  both static and dynamic mode; the result never depends on obstacle-set
365	  iteration order, in-frame coordinate order or the traversal order.
366	- ``max_cost`` caps a route's accumulated entering-cell cost exactly as
367	  in ``plan``: the start still costs 0, a candidate exactly at the
368	  limit still competes and a candidate whose accumulated cost would
369	  exceed it is discarded the moment it is generated. It never changes
370	  the tie-break between legal routes. ``max_expanded`` caps the number
371	  of complete route candidates actually closed (exactly what
372	  ``expanded`` counts); once the limit is reached no further candidate
373	  is closed, and the limit only ever truncates the traversal -- it can
374	  never replace an already determined higher-ranked route. When either
375	  limit is provided the result additionally carries ``status``:
376	  ``"found"`` when all ``k`` routes were closed or the search exhausted
377	  naturally with at least one route; ``"budget_exhausted"`` when fewer
378	  than ``k`` routes were found and the budget stopped the search while
379	  candidates were still pending (this wins when both limits fire);
380	  ``"cost_exhausted"`` when fewer than ``k`` routes were found, no
381	  budget stop occurred and at least one candidate was discarded for the
382	  cost limit; ``"unreachable"`` when no route exists with neither a
383	  budget stop nor a cost discard. The routes already closed (and their
384	  costs, in rank order) are still returned when a limit ends the search
385	  early, as empty lists when none were found, and ``expanded`` is the
386	  actual closed count. Omitting both limits keeps every legacy key and
387	  value exactly unchanged.
388	
389	Batch planning (``plan_batch``):
390	- ``plan_batch(width, height, blocked, requests, costs=None,
391	  trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
392	  max_cost=None, allow_wait=False, dynamic_costs=None)`` answers
393	  several independent single-goal queries on
394	  one shared grid in a single call. It returns ``{"results": [...]}``
395	  with exactly the result ``plan`` would return for each query, in the
396	  order of ``requests``; duplicate requests are kept and each gets its
397	  own result.
398	- The shared arguments are validated with ``plan``'s rules and order,
399	  with ``requests`` taking the position of ``start``/``goal`` in that
400	  sequence. ``requests`` must be a non-empty sequence: ``None``,
401	  strings, bytes and other non-sequences raise ``TypeError`` and an
402	  empty sequence raises ``ValueError``. Each element must be a
403	  two-element sequence ``[start, goal]`` of grid coordinates: element
404	  shape or coordinate type failures raise ``TypeError``; out-of-bounds
405	  coordinates, endpoints on static obstacles and a start blocked at
406	  dynamic frame 0 raise ``ValueError``. Every check is decided before
407	  any search starts, so an invalid batch never returns partial results.
408	- Each query is an independent ``plan`` search over the shared grid:
409	  ``path``, ``cost`` and ``expanded`` are produced per request, and the
410	  ``max_expanded`` budget and the ``max_cost`` limit apply per query
411	  with no state shared across queries. The optional ``dynamic_costs``
412	  frames follow the shared time-varying cost rules and are validated
413	  after every other check, before any request is searched; each request
414	  is then answered exactly as an independent ``plan`` call with the
415	  same frames, and a per-request checkpoint records them. ``trace``,
416	  ``status``,
417	  ``expanded_nodes``, ``checkpoint``, dynamic frames, ``start == goal``,
418	  unreachable and ``cost_exhausted`` results all follow ``plan``
419	  exactly, and a returned ``checkpoint`` can be handed to ``resume``
420	  directly. A successful path ends at its request's goal and verifies
421	  offline in ``replay`` with the same cost and step count. The result
422	  never depends on obstacle-set iteration order, in-frame coordinate
423	  order or the permutation of ``requests``.
424	
425	Multi-start planning (``plan_multi_start``):
426	- ``plan_multi_start(width, height, blocked, starts, goal, costs=None,
427	  trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
428	  max_cost=None, allow_wait=False, dynamic_costs=None)`` plans from
429	  several candidate starts to one shared
430	  goal in a single call and returns one deterministic route, in exactly
431	  the result structure of ``plan``; the path begins at the winning start
432	  and ends at ``goal``. ``starts`` takes ``start``'s position in
433	  ``plan``'s validation sequence and every shared check keeps its order,
434	  exception type and message boundary.
435	- ``starts`` must be a non-empty sequence of grid coordinates: ``None``,
436	  strings, bytes and other non-sequences raise ``TypeError`` and an
437	  empty sequence raises ``ValueError``. Each start follows the
438	  coordinate structure and integer rules (bad shape or coordinate types
439	  raise ``TypeError``); out-of-bounds coordinates and starts on static
440	  obstacles raise ``ValueError``. Repeated starts merge and the tuple is
441	  sorted, so the input ordering never changes any result. A start
442	  blocked by dynamic frame 0 raises ``ValueError``; every check runs
443	  before the search starts.
444	- In static mode every start is a ``g == 0`` root and each coordinate is
445	  closed at most once: a cell keeps only its best known ``(cost, path)``
446	  pair (smallest accumulated entering-cell cost, then the
447	  lexicographically smallest complete coordinate sequence -- an ordering
448	  preserved under common extensions, so a dominated candidate can never
449	  win later). In dynamic mode the persistent last frame, the ban on
450	  waiting and on repeated coordinates apply, and routes reaching the
451	  same ``(x, y, t)`` through different coordinate histories are distinct
452	  states that are never merged. Time-varying ``dynamic_costs`` frames
453	  (validated after every other check, before the search) make the
454	  search time-expanded the same way obstacle frames do: entering a
455	  coordinate at path index ``t`` costs that frame's cell value, the
456	  last frame persists, and the trace records ``(x, y, t)`` triples.
457	- The winning route has the smallest total ``cost``; ties are decided by
458	  the lexicographic order of the complete coordinate path, so the result
459	  never depends on the input order of ``starts``. Expansion order is f,
460	  then h, then ``(x, y)`` (plus ``t`` in dynamic mode), and finally the
461	  complete path. ``cost`` counts only the cells entered (the winning
462	  start costs 0); ``expanded`` counts only closed candidates; when no
463	  route exists ``path`` and ``cost`` are ``None``.
464	- With ``trace=True`` static mode records the unique coordinate closing
465	  sequence and dynamic mode the ``(x, y, t)`` closing sequence, and
466	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)``. A ``starts`` entry equal to
467	  ``goal`` yields the single-point zero-cost route under the same
468	  start-equals-goal and zero-budget rules as ``plan``.
469	- ``max_expanded`` and ``max_cost`` follow ``plan``'s ``status`` and
470	  budget-priority rules: a candidate whose accumulated cost would
471	  exceed ``max_cost`` is discarded without counting toward ``expanded``,
472	  and neither limit ever changes the unlimited route or the tie-breaks.
473	  With ``snapshot=True`` a budget stop returns a JSON-serializable
474	  checkpoint recording the sorted starts, the grid constraints, the
475	  dynamic frames, the time-varying cost frames when they were provided,
476	  the cost limit when one was provided and the complete
477	  pending state; ``resume`` continues it with the cumulative-budget,
478	  no-double-counting and only-budget-exhausted-snapshots rules of the
479	  other planners, and invalid checkpoints follow ``resume``'s usual
480	  ``TypeError``/``ValueError`` boundaries.
481	
482	Snapshots and resumable planning (``snapshot`` and ``resume``):
483	- ``plan`` and ``plan_any`` accept a final ``snapshot=False`` option.
484	  Omitting it or passing ``False`` keeps every key, value, exception type,
485	  validation order, tie-break, unreachable result and trace of the
486	  previous behavior untouched. A non-bool ``snapshot`` raises
487	  ``TypeError`` after all existing checks (the ``max_expanded`` validation
488	  included) and before the search starts.
489	- With ``snapshot=True``, a search that stops because ``max_expanded``
490	  was reached (``status == "budget_exhausted"``) additionally returns
491	  ``checkpoint``: a fully JSON-serializable snapshot of the planner state.
492	  Results that already found the goal or proved it unreachable never
493	  carry the field.
494	- The checkpoint records the snapshot version, the planner kind, the
495	  normalized grid constraints (dimensions, obstacles, start, goal or
496	  candidate goals, costs, dynamic frames and the cost limit when one was
497	  provided), the closed-node count, the
498	  trace recorded so far and the complete pending-candidate state. Every
499	  set-derived list is stored sorted, so neither obstacle-set iteration
500	  order, goal order nor in-frame coordinate order influences the
501	  checkpoint's keys or values. A caller may store it as-is and hand it
502	  back to ``resume`` later.
503	- ``resume(checkpoint, max_expanded=None)`` continues the very same
504	  deterministic search described by the snapshot. ``max_expanded`` keeps
505	  its cumulative meaning: the total number of nodes that may be closed
506	  counted from the original start, so a limit not greater than the
507	  already closed count closes nothing more. The result is equivalent to
508	  one uninterrupted call with the same cumulative budget: ``path``,
509	  ``cost``, ``expanded``, ``status`` (present exactly when
510	  ``max_expanded`` is given) and ``expanded_nodes`` (always present in
511	  resume results; coordinate pairs in static mode, ``(x, y, t)`` triples
512	  in dynamic mode) all match, and repeated resumes never count an already
513	  closed node twice.
514	- When a resumed search reaches the budget again its result carries a
515	  fresh ``checkpoint`` that can be resumed in turn; ``found`` and
516	  ``unreachable`` results omit it. A successful resumed ``path`` verifies
517	  in ``replay`` with the same cost and step count.
518	- Validation: a checkpoint that is not an object, has missing required
519	  fields or wrongly typed fields raises ``TypeError``; an unsupported
520	  snapshot version or planner kind, grid constraints that violate the
521	  usual ``plan`` rules (obstacles, endpoints, costs, dynamic frames) or
522	  an internally inconsistent state raise ``ValueError``. Every check is
523	  decided before any searching, and ``resume``'s ``max_expanded`` follows
524	  the same non-negative-integer rules as ``plan``'s.
525	
526	Offline replay (``replay``):
527	- ``replay`` re-checks a saved candidate path without running any search;
528	  it never returns ``expanded`` or ``expanded_nodes``. It accepts the same
529	  grid arguments as ``plan`` (no ``trace``) plus ``path``.
530	- The grid arguments are validated with exactly the public ``plan``
531	  checks, and all of them run before the path is judged, so the same
532	  malformed grid inputs raise the same ``TypeError``/``ValueError``.
533	- ``path`` must be a non-empty sequence of grid coordinates; strings,
534	  bytes, ``None`` and other non-sequences raise ``TypeError``, as do
535	  elements that are not exactly two integers. Coordinates outside the
536	  grid raise ``ValueError``.
537	- A structurally valid but semantically invalid path does not raise: it
538	  returns ``{"valid": False, "cost": None, "steps": None}`` with no
539	  partial accumulation. Invalid means: not beginning at ``start``, not
540	  ending at ``goal``, visiting a static obstacle, visiting a cell blocked
541	  by frame ``t`` at path index ``t`` (the last frame persists for later
542	  indices; omitted/empty ``dynamic_blocked`` means static-only checks),
543	  non-four-neighbor adjacency, repeated coordinates, or extra points when
544	  ``start == goal``.
545	- A valid path returns ``{"valid": True, "cost": int, "steps": int}``
546	  where ``steps == len(path) - 1`` and ``cost`` is recomputed with the
547	  same entering-cell rule ``plan`` uses (sum of the costs of the cells
548	  entered; unit costs without ``costs``; the start cell is never
549	  counted), so it equals the cost ``plan`` assigns to that same path.
550	- ``diagnose`` defaults to false; omitting it or passing ``False`` keeps
551	  every key, value, exception type and validation order identical. A
552	  non-bool ``diagnose`` raises ``TypeError`` after all grid checks
553	  (including the frame-0 check) and before the path structure is
554	  inspected. With ``diagnose=True`` both results additionally carry
555	  ``error`` and ``error_index``: ``None``/``None`` for a valid path, and
556	  for an invalid one a single error code plus the zero-based index of
557	  the first offending element, with ``cost``/``steps`` still ``None``.
558	  The codes, in fixed precedence order, are ``start_mismatch`` (index
559	  0), ``goal_mismatch`` (index of the last element),
560	  ``start_goal_extra`` (index 1), ``repeated_coordinate`` (the second
561	  occurrence), ``non_adjacent`` (the later element of the pair),
562	  ``static_blocked`` and ``dynamic_blocked`` (the offending element);
563	  ties resolve to the earliest rule in this list and no partial cost is
564	  ever returned.
565	
566	Distance field (``distance_field``):
567	- ``distance_field(width, height, blocked, goal, costs=None,
568	  trace=False)`` is an offline analysis entry point for the static grid:
569	  it accepts only the dimensions, the static obstacles, a single goal and
570	  optionally ``costs`` and ``trace`` -- no start, no dynamic obstacles, no
571	  search budget, no cost limit and no snapshot option. The dimensions,
572	  goal coordinate, obstacle and costs checks (structure, integer types,
573	  bounds, duplicate merging, goal-on-obstacle) follow ``plan``'s public
574	  rules and order for those shared arguments and all run before the
575	  search starts; ``trace`` must be a bool (``TypeError`` otherwise).
576	- It returns ``{"distances": ..., "expanded": int}`` where ``distances``
577	  is a height-by-width matrix indexed ``distances[y][x]``: ``None`` for
578	  obstacles and for cells that cannot reach the goal, ``0`` for the goal
579	  itself, and for every other reachable cell the minimum sum of the
580	  entering-cell costs along a four-neighborhood route from that cell to
581	  the goal (unit steps without ``costs``; with ``costs`` each move adds
582	  the cost of the cell entered, exactly as ``plan`` accumulates ``cost``,
583	  so a reachable ``plan`` start yields the same value ``plan`` reports
584	  as ``cost``). No reachable distance is ever negative and the matrix
585	  always matches the grid dimensions; the result is JSON-serializable.
586	- ``expanded`` counts exactly the reachable cells determined and closed
587	  once each, the goal included. The closing order is fully specified:
588	  smallest current distance first, then the ``(x, y)`` coordinate in
589	  lexicographic order, so neither the obstacle-set iteration order nor
590	  the costs layout traversal influences the matrix, the count or the
591	  trace. With ``trace=True`` the result additionally carries
592	  ``expanded_nodes``, the coordinate pairs in that closing order, and
593	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)``; the field is omitted entirely
594	  when ``trace`` is false or omitted.
595	
596	Multi-goal distance field (``distance_field_any``):
597	- ``distance_field_any(width, height, blocked, goals, costs=None,
598	  trace=False)`` is the multi-goal counterpart of ``distance_field``:
599	  one offline analysis returns the minimum-cost field to any of the
600	  candidate endpoints in a single pass. It accepts only the dimensions,
601	  the static obstacles, a non-empty ``goals`` sequence and optionally
602	  ``costs`` and ``trace`` -- no start, no dynamic obstacles, no search
603	  budget, no cost limit and no snapshot option, and it never produces a
604	  ``status`` field. The dimensions, obstacles, costs and trace checks
605	  follow ``distance_field``'s public rules and order, and ``goals`` is
606	  validated exactly like ``plan_any``'s: ``None``, strings, bytes and
607	  other non-sequences raise ``TypeError``, an empty sequence raises
608	  ``ValueError``, elements that are not exactly two non-bool integers
609	  raise ``TypeError``, and out-of-bounds coordinates or endpoints on
610	  static obstacles raise ``ValueError``. The goals checks occupy
611	  ``goal``'s position in ``distance_field``'s validation sequence,
612	  duplicates merge, and every check runs before the search starts, so
613	  the input permutation never changes any result.
614	- It returns ``{"distances": ..., "targets": ..., "expanded": int}``.
615	  ``distances`` is the same height-by-width matrix as
616	  ``distance_field``: ``None`` for obstacles and for cells that cannot
617	  reach any endpoint, ``0`` for every endpoint, and otherwise the
618	  minimum over the endpoints of the accumulated entering-cell cost
619	  along a four-neighborhood route (unit steps without ``costs``; with
620	  ``costs`` each move adds the cost of the cell entered, the start
621	  cell's own cost never counted, exactly as ``plan``/``plan_any`` and
622	  ``distance_field`` accumulate). A reachable ``plan_any`` start yields
623	  the same value ``plan_any`` reports as ``cost``.
624	- ``targets`` is a matrix of the same shape: a reachable cell records
625	  the coordinate tuple of the endpoint that wins it, every other
626	  position is ``None`` (obstacles and unreachable cells, exactly where
627	  ``distances`` is ``None``); endpoints record themselves. When several
628	  endpoints tie at the same minimum distance the winner is the endpoint
629	  with the lexicographically smallest ``(x, y)`` coordinate, so the
630	  choice never depends on goal order. The whole result is
631	  JSON-serializable.
632	- ``expanded`` counts every reachable cell closed for the first time,
633	  all endpoints included, exactly once each. The closing order is
634	  smallest distance first, then the ``(x, y)`` coordinate
635	  lexicographically. With ``trace=True`` the result additionally
636	  carries ``expanded_nodes`` -- the coordinate pairs in that order,
637	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)`` -- and the key is omitted
638	  entirely when ``trace`` is false or omitted.

640	Offline audit (``verify_trace``):
641	- ``verify_trace(width, height, blocked, start, goal, record, costs=None,
642	  dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False, max_cost=None,
643	  allow_wait=False, dynamic_costs=None, reservations=None)`` checks a
644	  saved ``plan`` result against the deterministic result the same
645	  arguments produce, without exposing the recomputation. ``record`` may
646	  be the dict a ``trace=True`` call returned or its JSON round-tripped
647	  equivalent: coordinates may be lists or tuples, key order is
648	  irrelevant and extra keys are ignored. The grid, endpoint, costs,
649	  dynamic-frame, waiting, budget, snapshot, cost-limit, time-varying
650	  cost and reservation arguments are validated first, in exactly
651	  ``plan``'s public order and with its exception types; only then is the
652	  record inspected, so a missing or malformed record never skips a grid
653	  or constraint error.
654	- The record must be an object carrying at least ``path``, ``cost``,
655	  ``expanded`` and ``expanded_nodes``; when the deterministic result
656	  carries ``status`` or ``checkpoint`` those are verified as well. A
657	  record that is not an object, lacks a required field, has a wrongly
658	  typed field or a wrongly shaped trajectory entry raises ``TypeError``;
659	  an out-of-bounds coordinate, a trajectory entry inconsistent with the
660	  static/dynamic mode the arguments select (a triple in static mode, a
661	  pair in dynamic mode, a negative time, or a state recorded twice by
662	  the static search) or an invalid checkpoint structure raises
663	  ``ValueError``. Every such check is decided before the audit search
664	  starts.
665	- A structurally legal record never raises: the audit recomputes the
666	  deterministic result (with the trace on) and reports exactly
667	  ``{"valid": bool, "mismatch": ..., "index": ...}``. The first
668	  differing field is reported in the fixed order ``path``, ``cost``,
669	  ``expanded``, ``expanded_nodes``, ``status``, ``checkpoint``; a path
670	  or trajectory difference also gives the zero-based index of the first
671	  differing element, every other difference reports ``index`` ``None``.
672	  A fully consistent record returns ``valid`` true with ``mismatch``
673	  and ``index`` both ``None``. The audit covers unreachable and
674	  ``start == goal`` results, cost matrices, time-varying costs, dynamic
675	  obstacles, waiting, reservations, budgets, cost limits and resumed
676	  searches (a ``resume`` record equals the uninterrupted call with the
677	  same cumulative budget); ``expanded_nodes`` only ever corresponds to
678	  actually closed, non-duplicated states. The result is
679	  JSON-serializable, the record is never modified or completed, and no
680	  recomputed value leaks into it.
681	
682	Validation (all performed before the search starts):
683	- ``width``/``height`` must be positive integers.
684	- ``start``, ``goal`` and every entry of ``blocked`` must be grid
685	  coordinates: sequences of exactly two integers (tuples, lists, etc.),
686	  normalized to tuples.
687	- ``goals`` (``plan_any`` and ``distance_field_any``) must be a
688	  non-empty sequence of grid coordinates following the same rules,
689	  normalized, deduplicated and order-independent.
690	- ``requests`` (``plan_batch``) must be a non-empty sequence of
691	  two-element ``[start, goal]`` coordinate pairs following the same
692	  coordinate rules, with the input order and duplicates preserved.
693	- ``costs`` may be omitted or ``None`` (unit costs). Otherwise it must be a
694	  sequence of ``height`` rows, each a sequence of ``width`` positive
695	  integers; strings/bytes, non-integer cells and booleans are rejected.
696	- ``dynamic_costs`` (``plan``, ``plan_any``, ``plan_batch``,
697	  ``plan_multi_start``, ``plan_k`` and ``replay``) may be
698	  omitted, ``None`` or an empty sequence. Otherwise it must be a
699	  sequence of frames, each frame a height-by-width matrix following the
700	  ``costs`` rules per frame; providing both ``costs`` and
701	  ``dynamic_costs`` raises ``ValueError``.
702	- ``reservations`` (``plan``, ``plan_any``, ``plan_batch``,
703	  ``plan_multi_start``, ``plan_k`` and ``replay``) may be
704	  omitted, ``None`` or an empty sequence. Otherwise it must be a
705	  sequence of non-empty coordinate paths; consecutive stays are kept,
706	  duplicate routes merge and the entry order never affects the result.
707	- ``trace`` must be a bool; non-bool values raise ``TypeError``.
708	- Type or structure violations raise ``TypeError``; non-positive
709	  dimensions, out-of-bounds coordinates, endpoints on obstacles, wrong
710	  matrix shape, or non-positive cell costs raise ``ValueError``.
711	- Duplicate blocked cells are merged without changing the result.
712	"""

735	    if not _is_int(value):
736	        raise TypeError(

738	        )

744	def _normalize_point(value, name):
745	    if isinstance(value, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(value, Sequence):
746	        raise TypeError(
747	            f"{name} must be a sequence of two integers, "
748	            f"got {type(value).__name__}"
749	        )
750	    if len(value) != 2:
751	        raise TypeError(
752	            f"{name} must contain exactly two coordinates, got {len(value)}"
753	        )
754	    x, y = value[0], value[1]
755	    if not _is_int(x) or not _is_int(y):
756	        raise TypeError(f"{name} coordinates must be integers, got {value!r}")
757	    return (x, y)

761	    x, y = point
762	    if not (0 <= x < width and 0 <= y < height):
763	        raise ValueError(
764	            f"{name} {point} is outside the {width}x{height} grid"

770	        raise TypeError(
771	            f"blocked must be an iterable of grid coordinates, "
772	            f"got {type(blocked).__name__}"
773	        )
774	    cells = set()
775	    for index, item in enumerate(blocked):
776	        name = f"blocked[{index}]"

975	def _reservation_frames(paths):
976	    # Compile normalized reservation paths into per-frame vertex and
977	    # directed-edge sets. A path's t-th coordinate occupies its vertex at
978	    # frame ``t``; past the final coordinate the last one persists, so
979	    # the last compiled frame (index ``R - 1`` with ``R`` the longest
980	    # path) doubles as the persistent tail, exactly like
981	    # ``dynamic_blocked``'s last frame. Frame ``t``'s edge set holds the
982	    # directed edges (p[t], p[t + 1]) of every path -- the move a
983	    # candidate makes between frames ``t`` and ``t + 1`` may not traverse
984	    # one of them in reverse. A stay or the persistent tail yields a
985	    # self-edge, which never constrains a moving candidate (its vertex is
986	    # reserved anyway).
987	    horizon = max(len(path) for path in paths)
988	    vertex_frames = []
989	    edge_frames = []
990	    for t in range(horizon):
991	        vertices = set()
992	        edges = set()
993	        for path in paths:
994	            current = path[t] if t < len(path) else path[-1]
995	            nxt = path[t + 1] if t + 1 < len(path) else path[-1]
996	            vertices.add(current)
997	            edges.add((current, nxt))
998	        vertex_frames.append(frozenset(vertices))
999	        edge_frames.append(frozenset(edges))
1000	    return vertex_frames, edge_frames

1003	def _goal_not_before(paths, goal):
1004	    # The earliest frame at which a route may enter ``goal`` and then
1005	    # occupy it forever, given that every path in ``paths`` keeps its own
1006	    # final coordinate past its last frame: the frame after the last one
1007	    # in which any of ``paths`` occupies the cell. ``None`` when no path
1008	    # ever occupies it (no extra constraint); ``float("inf")`` when it is
1009	    # some path's final coordinate, whose occupancy persists, so no
1010	    # arrival can ever be safe.
1011	    latest = None
1012	    for path in paths:
1013	        if path[-1] == goal:
1014	            return float("inf")
1015	        for t in range(len(path) - 1, -1, -1):
1016	            if path[t] == goal:
1017	                if latest is None or t > latest:
1018	                    latest = t
1019	                break
1020	    return None if latest is None else latest + 1

1024	    # The last frame index a wait may enter: waits are only generated
1025	    # while the next time step still lies within the provided frames,
1026	    # where ``dynamic_blocked`` and ``reservations`` each provide frames
1027	    # (``None`` when neither does, which disables waiting).
1028	    last = None

1031	    if vertex_frames is not None:

1033	        last = res_last if last is None else max(last, res_last)

1206	def _search_static(width, height, obstacles, start, goal, costs, trace,
1207	                   max_expanded, max_cost=None, snapshot=False,
1208	                   allow_wait=False, state=None):
1209	    """Classic static-grid A* (the ``plan`` search without frames).
1210	
1211	    Cells are merged by coordinate: the best known ``g`` per cell is kept
1212	    in ``g_score``, stale heap entries are skipped, and ``came_from``
1213	    reconstructs the cheapest route once the goal is closed. With
1214	    ``max_cost`` a candidate whose accumulated entering-cell cost would
1215	    exceed the limit is discarded instead of queued, and the search
1216	    remembers whether any discard happened (``cost_limited``) so a
1217	    failure can be reported as ``cost_exhausted``; the flag is part of
1218	    the snapshot state so a resumed search stays equivalent to one
1219	    uninterrupted call. With
1220	    ``snapshot=True`` a budget stop additionally returns a checkpoint of
1221	    the complete search state; ``state`` carries such a snapshot back in
1222	    so ``resume`` continues the identical traversal. The snapshot needs
1223	    the trace even when the caller did not ask for it, so nodes are
1224	    recorded whenever ``trace`` or ``snapshot`` is true.
1225	    """
1226	
1227	    def heuristic(point):
1228	        return abs(point[0] - goal[0]) + abs(point[1] - goal[1])
1229	
1230	    def step_cost(point):
1231	        # Cost of entering ``point``; the start cell is never entered.
1232	        if costs is None:
1233	            return 1
1234	        return costs[point[1]][point[0]]

1236	    if state is None:
1237	        # Heap entries are (f, h, x, y, point): the first four fields give
1238	        # a total, input-order-independent ordering, so the point itself
1239	        # is never compared.
1240	        h0 = heuristic(start)
1241	        open_heap = [(h0, h0, start[0], start[1], start)]
1242	        came_from = {}
1243	        g_score = {start: 0}
1244	        closed = set()
1245	        expanded_nodes = [] if trace or snapshot else None
1246	        cost_limited = False
1247	    else:
1248	        open_heap = state["open"]
1249	        came_from = state["came_from"]
1250	        g_score = state["g_score"]
1251	        closed = state["closed"]
1252	        expanded_nodes = state["expanded_nodes"]
1253	        cost_limited = state["cost_limited"]

1255	    has_status = max_expanded is not None or max_cost is not None
1256	
1257	    while open_heap:
1258	        entry = heapq.heappop(open_heap)
1259	        current = entry[4]
1260	        if current in closed:
1261	            continue  # stale heap entry; already closed with its best g
1262	        if max_expanded is not None and len(closed) >= max_expanded:

1264	            # nothing more (this also covers start == goal with a zero
1265	            # budget: no node is closed and no start is fabricated). The
1266	            # popped candidate was already removed from the heap, so for a
1267	            # snapshot it is pushed back: the checkpoint must hold every
1268	            # still-live candidate for the search to resume exactly.
1269	            budget_stop = True
1270	            if snapshot:
1271	                heapq.heappush(open_heap, entry)

1275	            expanded_nodes.append(current)

1277	            path = [current]
1278	            while path[-1] in came_from:
1279	                path.append(came_from[path[-1]])

1281	            result = {
1282	                "path": path,
1283	                "cost": g_score[current],
1284	                "expanded": len(closed),
1285	            }
1286	            if has_status:
1287	                result["status"] = "found"
1288	            if trace:
1289	                result["expanded_nodes"] = expanded_nodes

1291	        for dx, dy in _NEIGHBORS:
1292	            nxt = (current[0] + dx, current[1] + dy)
1293	            if not (0 <= nxt[0] < width and 0 <= nxt[1] < height):

1295	            if nxt in obstacles:
1296	                continue

1299	                if max_cost is not None and new_g > max_cost:
1300	                    # The candidate's accumulated cost exceeds the limit:
1301	                    # discard it and remember that a discard happened.
1302	                    cost_limited = True
1303	                    continue
1304	                g_score[nxt] = new_g
1305	                came_from[nxt] = current
1306	                h = heuristic(nxt)
1307	                heapq.heappush(
1308	                    open_heap, (new_g + h, h, nxt[0], nxt[1], nxt)
1309	                )

1311	    if has_status:
1312	        result["status"] = _status_for(budget_stop, cost_limited)
1313	    if trace:
1314	        result["expanded_nodes"] = expanded_nodes
1315	    if snapshot and result.get("status") == "budget_exhausted":

1320	                                   cost_limited, max_cost),

1326	def _search_dynamic(width, height, obstacles, frames, start, goal, costs,
1327	                    trace, max_expanded, max_cost=None, snapshot=False,
1328	                    allow_wait=False, state=None, cost_frames=None,
1329	                    reservations=None, goal_not_before=None):

1332	    Frame ``t`` constrains the cell occupied at path index ``t``; frames
1333	    past the last one reuse the last frame. ``frames`` may be ``None``
1334	    when ``cost_frames`` or ``reservations`` is given: time-varying costs
1335	    or reserved routes alone already make the search space time-expanded.
1336	    With ``cost_frames`` the price of
1337	    entering a cell at time ``t`` is that frame's cell value (frames past
1338	    the last one reuse the last frame); the start cell is never counted.
1339	    With ``reservations`` (normalized reservation paths) a candidate
1340	    route may not enter a vertex another agent occupies at the same
1341	    frame, nor traverse the reverse of a reserved directed edge between
1342	    two frames; reserved vertices persist at each path's final
1343	    coordinate. Waiting in place (unless ``allow_wait`` is set) and repeated
1344	    coordinates are forbidden, so
1345	    whether a candidate route can be
1346	    extended depends on the exact sequence of cells it already visited:
1347	    two routes reaching the same ``(x, y, t)`` with different histories
1348	    are distinct states and neither may prune the other (the route with
1349	    the larger accumulated cost can be the only one that remains
1350	    extendable). Each heap node therefore carries its complete path; the
1351	    search is a best-first traversal of the feasible route tree. Goal
1352	    closings are collected until the heap's smallest f exceeds the best
1353	    goal cost, after which the minimum-cost goal tie-break is settled by
1354	    the fixed f, h, x, y, t priority and then the complete path's
1355	    lexicographic order. With ``max_cost`` a candidate route whose
1356	    accumulated entering-cell cost would exceed the limit is discarded
1357	    (``cost_limited`` records that any discard happened, so a failure can
1358	    be reported as ``cost_exhausted``; the flag is part of the snapshot
1359	    state). With ``allow_wait`` a route may also stay in its current cell
1360	    for one frame at no entering-cell cost, generated only while the next
1361	    time step still lies within the provided frames and the cell is free
1362	    there; consecutive waits repeat the coordinate in the path, and once
1363	    a cell is left it may never be re-entered. With ``goal_not_before``
1364	    (used by ``plan_agents``) a route may not enter the goal cell before
1365	    that frame, because a reserved route still occupies it at some later
1366	    frame and the goal cell stays occupied once the route ends; such
1367	    candidates are never generated, exactly like reserved vertices.
1368	    With ``snapshot=True`` a
1369	    budget stop additionally
1370	    returns a checkpoint of the complete route-tree state; ``state``
1371	    carries such a snapshot back in for ``resume``.
1372	    """
1373	
1374	    def heuristic(point):
1375	        return abs(point[0] - goal[0]) + abs(point[1] - goal[1])
1376	
1377	    last_frame = len(frames) - 1 if frames is not None else None
1378	    last_cost_frame = len(cost_frames) - 1 if cost_frames is not None else None
1379	
1380	    def step_cost(point, t):
1381	        # Cost of entering ``point`` at time ``t``; the start cell is
1382	        # never entered. Time-varying frames take the value of frame
1383	        # ``t`` (the last frame persists); otherwise the static ``costs``
1384	        # matrix or unit steps apply.
1385	        if cost_frames is not None:
1386	            frame = (cost_frames[t] if t <= last_cost_frame
1387	                     else cost_frames[last_cost_frame])
1388	            return frame[point[1]][point[0]]

1390	            return 1
1391	        return costs[point[1]][point[0]]
1392	
1393	    def frame_cells(t):
1394	        if frames is None:
1395	            return frozenset()
1396	        return frames[t] if t <= last_frame else frames[last_frame]
1397	
1398	    if reservations is not None:
1399	        vertex_frames, edge_frames = _reservation_frames(reservations)
1400	        last_res_frame = len(vertex_frames) - 1
1401	    else:
1402	        vertex_frames = edge_frames = last_res_frame = None

1404	    def reserved_vertices(t):
1405	        # Cells another agent occupies at frame ``t``; the final
1406	        # coordinate of every reservation path persists.
1407	        if vertex_frames is None:
1408	            return frozenset()
1409	        return (vertex_frames[t] if t <= last_res_frame
1410	                else vertex_frames[last_res_frame])
1411	
1412	    def reserved_edges(t):
1413	        # Directed edges (a, b) another agent traverses between frames
1414	        # ``t`` and ``t + 1``; a candidate may not move from ``b`` to
1415	        # ``a`` on that transition.
1416	        if edge_frames is None:
1417	            return frozenset()
1418	        return (edge_frames[t] if t <= last_res_frame
1419	                else edge_frames[last_res_frame])

1422	    # reservation frames each provide them.
1423	    wait_last = _wait_horizon(frames, vertex_frames)
1424	
1425	    # Heap entries are (f, h, x, y, t, g, path, seen): f/h/x/y/t give the
1426	    # fixed numeric priority and candidates still tied are ordered by the
1427	    # complete coordinate path lexicographically, so ordering never depends
1428	    # on obstacle sets, in-frame coordinate order, or traversal order. The
1429	    # frozenset ``seen`` mirrors ``path`` for an O(1) repeat check and is
1430	    # never compared (distinct histories always differ in ``path``).
1431	    if state is None:
1432	        h0 = heuristic(start)
1433	        start_path = (start,)
1434	        if reservations is not None and start in reserved_vertices(0):
1435	            # The root itself would occupy a reserved vertex at frame 0,
1436	            # so no feasible route exists.
1437	            open_heap = []
1438	        elif goal_not_before is not None and start == goal:
1439	            # The single-point route would occupy the goal cell from
1440	            # frame 0 on, but a reserved route still needs it later.
1441	            open_heap = []
1442	        else:
1443	            open_heap = [(h0, h0, start[0], start[1], 0, 0, start_path,
1444	                          frozenset(start_path))]
1445	        closed_count = 0
1446	        expanded_nodes = [] if trace or snapshot else None
1447	        cost_limited = False
1448	        # Best goal closing seen so far, keyed exactly as the tie-break
1449	        # specializes at the goal: (g, t, path) (there f == g, h == 0 and
1450	        # (x, y) is fixed). Closing a goal does not stop the search
1451	        # immediately: an equally cheap route whose chain runs through
1452	        # higher-h nodes might still be undeveloped. Since each move costs
1453	        # at least 1 and the Manhattan h changes by at most 1 per move,
1454	        # f = g + h never decreases along a route; once the smallest f on
1455	        # the heap exceeds the best goal cost, no route of that cost (or

1459	        open_heap = state["open"]
1460	        closed_count = state["closed_count"]
1461	        expanded_nodes = state["expanded_nodes"]
1462	        best_key = state["best_key"]
1463	        cost_limited = state["cost_limited"]

1465	    has_status = max_expanded is not None or max_cost is not None

1468	        if best_key is not None and open_heap[0][0] > best_key[0]:
1469	            break
1470	        if max_expanded is not None and closed_count >= max_expanded:
1471	            # Live route candidates remain but the budget is spent; close
1472	            # nothing more. A goal already closed still wins below.
1473	            budget_stop = True
1474	            break

1477	        if expanded_nodes is not None:
1478	            # Histories reaching the same (x, y, t) each record a triple,

1484	                best_key = goal_key

1486	        next_t = t + 1
1487	        frame = frame_cells(next_t)
1488	        reserved = reserved_vertices(next_t)

1490	            nx, ny = x + dx, y + dy
1491	            if not (0 <= nx < width and 0 <= ny < height):
1492	                continue
1493	            nxt = (nx, ny)
1494	            if nxt in obstacles or nxt in frame or nxt in seen:

1496	            if nxt in reserved:
